title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit/Open
plain: The fuel volume regulator is a small electric valve, usually on the high-pressure fuel pump, that meters how much fuel is sent to the injectors. The computer has seen an open or broken connection in its control circuit. It is mostly found on diesels and some direct-injection gas engines.
symptoms: Engine may stall, lose power or go into limp mode

causes.name: Damaged, chafed or corroded wiring to the regulator
Loose or corroded connector at the regulator
Failed fuel volume regulator (open or shorted coil)
Engine computer driver fault

checks: Inspect the regulator connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Measure the regulator coil resistance and compare to spec
Check the power and control signal at the connector
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new fuel volume regulator if its coil has failed.

title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The fuel volume regulator is a small electric valve, usually on the high-pressure fuel pump, that meters how much fuel is sent to the injectors. The computer has seen a reading that does not match what it commanded in its control circuit. It is mostly found on diesels and some direct-injection gas engines.
symptoms: Engine may stall, lose power or go into limp mode

causes.name: Contaminated or low-quality fuel making the regulator stick
Faulty fuel volume regulator
Clogged fuel filter or low supply pressure
Worn high-pressure fuel pump
Damaged wiring or loose connector

checks: Replace the fuel filter if it is due and check for water in the fuel
Check low-side fuel supply pressure
Compare commanded and actual rail pressure with a scan tool
fix: Often a new fuel filter and, if needed, a new fuel volume regulator. A worn high-pressure pump is the less common but costlier cause.

title: Fuel Shutoff Valve "A" Control Circuit/Open
plain: Some engines, mostly diesels, have an electric fuel shutoff valve that opens to let the engine run and closes to stop it. The computer has seen an open or broken connection in the wiring that controls this valve.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may stall
Engine may not shut off right away when the key is turned off

causes.name: Damaged or corroded wiring to the shutoff valve
Loose or corroded connector
Failed fuel shutoff valve solenoid
Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the valve
Engine computer driver fault

checks: Check the fuse and relay for the fuel shutoff circuit
Inspect the valve connector and wiring
Test the solenoid resistance and operation
fix: Repair the wiring or connector, or replace the fuel shutoff solenoid if it has failed.

title: Engine Position System Performance (Bank 1)
plain: The computer compares the crankshaft and camshaft sensor signals and found that the timing between them on bank 1 is off. On many engines this points to a stretched timing chain.
symptoms: Rattle from the front of the engine at startup
Hard starting or lower fuel economy

causes.name: Stretched timing chain
Low oil level or overdue oil changes speeding up chain wear
Worn timing chain guides or tensioner
Faulty camshaft actuator or oil control valve
Faulty crankshaft or camshaft sensor

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Look for related codes such as P0009, P0016 to P0019
Have a shop check cam-to-crank deviation values with a scan tool
fix: Usually a timing chain set with guides and tensioners. Keeping up with oil changes helps prevent it from coming back.
examples: Very well known on the GM 3.6L V6 (Chevrolet Traverse, Equinox, GMC Acadia, Cadillac CTS) from roughly 2007 to 2012

title: Engine Position System Performance (Bank 2)
plain: The computer compares the crankshaft and camshaft sensor signals and found that the timing between them on bank 2 is off. This often means the timing chain has stretched.
symptoms: Rough idle or rattle at startup
Possible loss of power or fuel economy

causes.name: Stretched timing chain
Low oil level or long oil change intervals
Worn timing chain guides or tensioner
Faulty camshaft or crankshaft sensor

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Check for related codes such as P0008 or P0016 to P0019
Have cam-to-crank deviation values checked with a scan tool
fix: Usually a timing chain set with guides and tensioners.
examples: Often sets along with P0008 on the GM 3.6L V6 when the timing chains stretch

title: "A" Camshaft Position Slow Response (Bank 1)
plain: The variable valve timing system moves the "A" (usually intake) camshaft on bank 1 to change engine timing. The computer saw the camshaft take too long to reach the position it asked for.

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong-grade engine oil
Sticking camshaft oil control valve (VVT solenoid)
Worn camshaft phaser
Stretched timing chain

checks: Check the oil level and change oil if it is dirty or overdue
Inspect the oil control valve and its screen for sludge
Check for other cam timing codes
fix: Often an oil change with the correct oil, then a new oil control valve if the code returns. A worn phaser or chain is less common.

title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit
plain: The computer constantly adjusts the fuel volume regulator to keep fuel pressure right. It has had to adjust it further than allowed, which means something in the fuel system is not behaving normally.
symptoms: Possible hard starting or rough running

causes.name: Worn or sticking fuel volume regulator
Clogged fuel filter or low supply pressure
Worn high-pressure fuel pump
Faulty fuel rail pressure sensor

checks: Check and replace the fuel filter if needed
Compare commanded and actual fuel rail pressure with a scan tool
Check low-side fuel supply pressure
fix: Usually a fuel filter and, if needed, a new fuel volume regulator.

title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated
plain: High-pressure fuel systems have a safety relief valve that opens if fuel pressure climbs too high. The computer has detected that this valve opened.
symptoms: Engine may lose power, stumble or stall

causes.name: Fuel pressure regulator or volume regulator stuck
Faulty fuel rail pressure sensor giving a false high reading
Worn or leaking pressure relief valve
Wiring fault in the pressure control circuit

checks: Check for other fuel pressure codes
Compare commanded and actual rail pressure with a scan tool
Inspect wiring to the rail pressure sensor and regulator
fix: Find out why pressure went too high, usually a stuck regulator or a bad pressure sensor, and replace that part. The relief valve may also need replacing.

title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
plain: The engine uses an electric oil control valve to adjust the "A" (usually intake) camshaft timing on bank 1. The computer found a problem in the wiring or the valve itself, such as an open or shorted circuit.
symptoms: Engine may run fine but with a light on

causes.name: Failed camshaft oil control valve (VVT solenoid)
Damaged wiring or loose connector at the solenoid
Oil leaking into the solenoid connector
Engine computer driver fault

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector for oil, corrosion or a loose fit
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
Command the solenoid on with a scan tool and watch for a response
fix: Usually a new camshaft oil control valve, or a wiring or connector repair.

cost.job: Replace camshaft oil control valve (VVT solenoid)

title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
plain: The "A" (usually intake) camshaft on bank 1 is further ahead of, or not following, the position the computer asked for. The variable valve timing system is not controlling it correctly.
symptoms: Possible stalling or rattle at startup

causes.name: Low, dirty or wrong-grade engine oil
Sticking or failed camshaft oil control valve
Camshaft phaser stuck or worn
Stretched timing chain or jumped timing
Clogged oil screen at the oil control valve

checks: Check the oil level and change it if dirty or overdue, using the correct grade
Remove and inspect the oil control valve for sludge or a stuck spool
Check cam timing values with a scan tool before replacing the phaser or chain
fix: Start with an oil change. If it comes back, the oil control valve is the most common fix, then the phaser or timing chain.

cost.job: Replace camshaft oil control valve (VVT solenoid)

examples: Often linked to low or dirty oil on engines with variable valve timing, such as the GM 2.4L Ecotec and many Toyota four-cylinders

title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)

fix: Start with an oil change. If it comes back, the oil control valve is the most common fix, then the phaser or timing chain.

cost.job: Replace camshaft oil control valve (VVT solenoid)

examples: Common on the Ford 5.4L 3-valve V8 (F-150, Expedition) when the cam phasers wear

title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
plain: The crankshaft and camshaft must stay in exact step. The computer compared their sensor signals and found the timing between the crank and the "A" (usually intake) camshaft on bank 1 is out of the expected range.
symptoms: Rough idle, misfire or loss of power
Rattle from the timing chain area at startup

causes.name: Stretched timing chain or worn chain tensioner
Timing chain or belt jumped a tooth
Faulty camshaft or crankshaft position sensor
Sticking oil control valve or worn cam phaser
Damaged reluctor (tone) ring or sensor wiring problem

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Check the sensor wiring and connectors
Have a shop check cam/crank sync with a scope or scan tool before replacing the timing chain
fix: Often a timing chain, tensioner and guides. Sometimes it is just a camshaft or crankshaft sensor, so test before replacing major parts.
examples: Well known on VW and Audi 2.0T TSI engines with a failing timing chain tensioner
Also seen on the GM 3.6L V6 and Mercedes M272 V6 with timing-related wear

title: "A" Camshaft Profile Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
plain: Some engines can switch between two camshaft lobe shapes, one for economy and one for power. The computer found an open or broken connection in the control circuit for this switching on bank 1.
symptoms: Less power at higher engine speeds
Engine may stay in one cam mode

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector to the cam profile solenoid
Failed cam profile switching solenoid
Low or dirty engine oil affecting the switching mechanism
Engine computer driver fault

checks: Check the oil level and condition
Inspect the solenoid connector and wiring
Test the solenoid resistance and command it with a scan tool
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new cam profile switching solenoid.
